items.title: Louis Gallaud Interview, 1960-03-18
items.q: Sometime if Rainier's band wasn't playing, well, sometimes they'd use Raymond Rainier's men because men were so short at that time.

ctx.x: When did you first hear that word, the jazz? When did they start using that, do you know?

Well, they used to say, kid punch jazz band on the program, you know, when they advertised the band at that time. Yeah. You see, kid punchin' his jazz boys or kid punchin' his jazz band. But sometime if Rainier's band wasn't playing, well, sometimes they'd use Raymond Rainier's men because men were so short at that time. Sometime when Sam Morgan would get short, well, he'd use some of them men when they wasn't playing. But when they was playing, well, they had to use what they could at that time because they…

Well, I was going to ask in the very beginning about if you ever had any lessons on the piano. You said that Rene and people helped you some. Oh, yeah. Did you ever take lessons on the piano with a book and a picture?
